learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Knowledge and understanding: Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods appropriately and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems of their specialty, that comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Engineering projects: Project ability using some cutting-edge knowledge of their engineering specialty.

Research and innovation: Ability to conduct bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers and people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Ability to recognize the need for their own continuous training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Continuous training: Ability to stay updated on new developments in science and technology.
Define the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each of them, and making correct use of language, in writing.

syllabus_topics: The need for electric drives and the importance of a good selection of them
Characteristics: rotating flux, slip, connection terminals
Power diagrams: direct start, direction change, star-delta start
Analysis of various industrial applications and the selection of drives for them
teaching_methods: Development, drafting, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Teacher presentations in participatory classroom sessions of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and/or control points

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, presentation and technical defense
Written and oral individual tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment and project feedback are applied. Students must meet regularly with experts to monitor the project and ensure objective achievement. For theory, the grade for asynchronous motors, AC servo motors, and industrial applications is calculated as 0.25 * 1st Control Point + 0.75 * recovery control point. Group exercises do not have a recovery option, and project recovery involves continuous assessment and feedback.
